terms.definition: The interaction of a community of living organisms (biotic) with the non-living (abiotic) parts of their environment.
terms.examiner: A community is all the populations in a habitat.

terms.definition: All the organisms of one species living in a habitat.
Species depend on each other for food, shelter, pollination and seed dispersal; removing one can affect the whole community.
terms.examiner: A stable community has species and environmental factors in balance.

terms.definition: A non-living factor such as light intensity, temperature, moisture, soil pH and mineral content, wind, carbon dioxide or oxygen.
A living factor such as food availability, new predators, new pathogens or competition.
terms.examiner: One species out-competing another can reduce its numbers.

terms.definition: A feature that helps an organism survive in its environment: structural, behavioural or functional.
terms.examiner: Give the feature and how it helps survival.

terms.definition: An organism that lives in extreme conditions, such as high temperature, pressure or salt concentration.
terms.examiner: Bacteria in deep-sea vents are extremophiles.
